QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_19

question.text: For the AB Responsible Services IWMP case, the workbook lists "177 hectares of land brought under irrigation". Applying the workbook's own definition on p. 22 — that outputs are the readily-measured, immediate consequences of the project's activities (the physical things the activities deliver) — and noting that yield change would be the outcome and farmer income / food security would be the impact, which of the following is the BEST classification of "177 hectares brought under irrigation" along the input -> output -> outcome -> impact ladder?

explanation.text: The Logic: SIA workbook p. 22 defines outputs as readily-measured immediate consequences of the project's activities — the physical things activities deliver. "Hectares brought under irrigation" is a physical, directly-measured deliverable of watershed-development activities, which fits the output definition. Yield change (productivity) would be the OUTCOME, and farmer income / food security would be the IMPACT. The Trap: Option A confuses output with input (inputs are the resources used — capital, labour, materials). Options B and C are downstream stages in the result chain. The audit flagged the original because the IWMP case on p. 167 calls 177 hectares irrigated a "quantitative key impact indicator", which can lead candidates toward option B if read literally. On the workbook's own definitions (p. 22), however, that metric is an output deliverable, not an impact-stage measure. Note: The original stem did not cite the p. 22 definitions and did not flag the wording mismatch with p. 167's "key impact indicator" phrase. The stem now explicitly grounds the classification in the p. 22 definitions and contrasts output with outcome (yield) and impact (income / food security), making option D uniquely correct on the workbook's own definitional framework.
